title: Qwen3: Hybrid Thinking, Open Weights
hook: Qwen3 puts a reasoning switch in one model - a slow 'thinking' mode and a fast 'non-thinking' mode with a controllable budget - across a lineup that runs from 0.6B to a 235B MoE.
key_points: Hybrid design: a 'thinking' mode for step-by-step reasoning and a fast 'non-thinking' mode, with a controllable reasoning budget.
Dense models at 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, and 32B, plus two MoE models: Qwen3-30B-A3B and flagship Qwen3-235B-A22B (235B total / 22B active).
Pretrained on roughly 36 trillion tokens, about twice the budget of Qwen2.5.
Released under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, and Qwen Chat.
content_html: Alibaba's Qwen Team released Qwen3 in April 2025, an open-weight family whose headline feature is hybrid reasoning: a single model can run in a deliberate "thinking" mode or a fast "non-thinking" mode, with a budget you can dial up or down. The lineup spans small dense models up to a 235B mixture-of-experts flagship, all under the Apache 2.0 license.
extra_html:
What's new

Rather than shipping a separate reasoning model, Qwen3 folds both behaviors into one: "thinking" mode works through problems step by step, while "non-thinking" mode answers quickly, and a controllable reasoning budget lets you trade latency for depth. The family includes dense models at 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, and 32B, plus two MoE models - Qwen3-30B-A3B and the flagship Qwen3-235B-A22B, with 235B total parameters and 22B active. It was pretrained on roughly 36 trillion tokens, about double Qwen2.5, and supports 119 languages.

Why it matters

A single model that toggles between fast answers and slow reasoning simplifies deployment, and the open Apache 2.0 license plus broad distribution - Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, and Qwen Chat - keeps Qwen among the most accessible frontier-class open families. See the Qwen blog for the full lineup.

related.title: Qwen2-VL: Vision-Language at Any Resolution
related.hook: Qwen2-VL processes images at their native resolution rather than forcing a fixed size, making it significantly better at reading small text and understanding fine-grained visual detail.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.
